title: Pepper-sprayed man had broken bones, inquest hears
article: An autopsy showed that a Regina man who died in 2008 after being subdued by police had a number of broken bones, a coroner's inquest heard Tuesday.
Calvin McLean, 43, died after he struggled with police officers and was pepper-sprayed - and then went into medical distress.
At the inquest into his death Tuesday, a jury learned about a number of other injuries he received.
Several police officers testified and were questioned by McLean family lawyer Bob Hrycan.
During questioning, Hrycan referred to an autopsy report that said McLean had eight broken ribs.
At one point, during the Oct. 8 struggle, five officers had pinned McLean to the ground.
Once McLean was subdued and brought to his knees, there was a pool of blood on the ground, on the sidewalk where his head was, the jury heard.
There was also blood around his mouth and he was unresponsive. McLean was unable to respond to his rights and warnings.
CPR was administered to him, but he died the next day.
Hrycan questioned whether police used more force than was necessary.
"He had eight cracked ribs, four cracks on each side and he had a broken sternum," Hrycan told CBC News during a break in the inquest.
"Obviously, we will be posing questions to the pathologist about the amount of force required to cause all those injuries."
Police were called after receiving a report of a man waving an axe. They thought McLean was armed and said he resisted arrest.

"The broken bones speak for themselves," Hrycan said. "You shouldn't have to cause that degree of injury to an individual to achieve an arrest. They never found any weapons on him. He never threatened any of the officers. He never wounded any of the officers and he never struck any of the officers."
The inquest is trying to determine the circumstances surrounding the Oct. 9, 2008 death.
The jury can also make recommendations to prevent similar deaths in the future. The inquest began Monday and is scheduled to wrap up Friday.
